/conditions/hip-arthritis/treatment.answer: UK first-line care for hip osteoarthritis is exercise, weight support where needed, and simple pain relief — not an early rush to replacement. Surgery is considered when sleep, walking and daily tasks stay badly limited after months of conservative care.
/conditions/hip-arthritis/treatment.bodyHtml:
UK first-line care for hip osteoarthritis is exercise, weight support where needed, and simple pain relief — not an early rush to replacement. Surgery is considered when sleep, walking and daily tasks stay badly limited after months of conservative care.

Treatment approaches

Exercise and physiotherapy

Glute and hip-abductor strength plus low-impact cardio are core NICE-aligned treatment for everyone with hip OA.

Weight management

The hip takes roughly three times body weight when walking, so even modest weight loss can cut load and pain.

Pain relief

Paracetamol, topical NSAIDs, and short courses of oral NSAIDs for flares if safe for you.

Walking aids

A stick in the opposite hand, or a pole, can offload a painful hip on longer walks.

Steroid injection

Sometimes used for a severe flare while rehabilitation continues — not a permanent fix.

Hip replacement

Considered when pain disturbs sleep, limits daily life, and 3–6 months of conservative care has not been enough.

NHS pathway in plain English

Most people start with a GP or first-contact physiotherapist. Core treatment is a supervised exercise plan and, where relevant, support with weight. If night pain, limp and walking distance stay poor after a proper conservative trial, you may be referred to an MSK or hip clinic to discuss imaging and, later, replacement. NICE does not treat replacement as a first visit.

Walking aids and sleep

A stick in the opposite hand reduces load on the painful hip on longer walks. If night pain wakes you when you lie on that side, a pillow between the knees and not sleeping on the sore hip is a practical first step while you wait for physiotherapy. Persistent night pain after these changes is a reason to go back to the GP, not to search for a hip-replacement clinic on the first week of symptoms.

faqs.q: What is the first treatment for hip osteoarthritis on the NHS?
faqs.a: NICE-aligned care starts with exercise, weight support where needed, and simple pain relief — not an early hip replacement. Physiotherapy for glutes and hip abductors plus a low-impact cardio choice is core treatment for everyone.

faqs.q: Do I need a hip replacement?
faqs.a: Replacement is considered when sleep, walking and daily tasks stay badly limited after months of conservative care. It is a later conversation, not the default first appointment.

faqs.q: Does a walking stick help hip arthritis?
faqs.a: Yes for many people on longer walks. Use the stick in the opposite hand to the painful hip so it offloads that side. A pole can do the same job outdoors.

faqs.q: Are steroid injections a cure for hip OA?
faqs.a: No. An image-guided hip injection can settle a bad flare while you keep rehabilitating. Relief is temporary. Ask a clinician whether it fits your other health conditions.

faqs.q: Can I use ibuprofen gel on the hip?
faqs.a: Topical NSAIDs are first-line for some joints in NICE OA guidance. The hip sits deeper than a finger joint, so gel may help less than it does for a knee or hand. Oral NSAIDs, if appropriate, are short courses with food after a pharmacist or GP check.

/conditions/hip-arthritis/exercises.title: Best Exercises for Hip Arthritis: Safe UK Physio-Aligned Routines | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/hip-arthritis/exercises.description: Safe, effective hip arthritis exercises aligned with UK physiotherapy guidance. Movements to try, exercises to avoid, and how to build a weekly routine.
/conditions/hip-arthritis/exercises.question: Best exercises for hip arthritis
/conditions/hip-arthritis/exercises.answer: NICE lists exercise as a core treatment for hip osteoarthritis. Strength work for the glutes and hip abductors plus swimming, cycling or pool walking usually beats rest.
/conditions/hip-arthritis/exercises.bodyHtml:
NICE lists exercise as a core treatment for hip osteoarthritis. Strength work for the glutes and hip abductors plus swimming, cycling or pool walking usually beats rest.

Key benefits

  • Reduces groin and outer-hip pain with consistent practice
  • Improves ability to stand from a chair and climb stairs
  • Supports the muscles that stabilise a worn hip joint
  • Low-impact options (pool, bike) keep fitness without heavy joint load
  • Helps before and after any planned hip replacement

Use the written hip routine

This site keeps a full eight-move hip osteoarthritis routine on the dedicated hip-exercise guide. Open that guide for the step-by-step set. This page is the short version: glutes, abductors, and a low-impact cardio choice you can repeat most weeks.

What to skip during a flare

Deep loaded squats, long downhill walks, and stretching into sharp groin catch usually worsen a flare. Switch to pool walking or a bike, keep the range comfortable, and return to strength when night pain eases.

faqs.q: What are the best exercises for hip osteoarthritis?
faqs.a: Glute and hip-abductor strength plus swimming, cycling or pool walking. This site’s dedicated hip-exercise guide has a full step-by-step routine. Rest alone usually makes the hip stiffer.

faqs.q: Is walking good for hip arthritis?
faqs.a: Steady walking on even ground is useful for many people. Hills, long downhill stretches and deep loaded squats often flare groin pain. If walking aggravates you, switch to a bike or pool and keep the strength work.

faqs.q: What exercises should I avoid with a painful hip?
faqs.a: Skip deep loaded squats early, lunges that catch in the groin, and stretching into sharp pain. A pole in the opposite hand can offload a painful hip on walks.

faqs.q: How often should I exercise with hip OA?
faqs.a: Most days, in short blocks. Two or three strength sessions a week plus regular low-impact cardio is a realistic UK pattern. Benefits build over weeks, not after one gym visit.

faqs.q: Can I exercise before a hip replacement?
faqs.a: Yes — stronger glutes and better walking stamina usually help recovery. Keep the range comfortable and follow the plan your physiotherapy team gives you.

/conditions/hip-arthritis/diet.title: Best Diet for Hip Arthritis: Anti-Inflammatory Foods to Eat & Avoid (UK) | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/hip-arthritis/diet.description: What to eat — and what to limit — with hip arthritis. UK-aligned anti-inflammatory diet guidance, food triggers, and the supplements with the best evidence.
/conditions/hip-arthritis/diet.question: Diet for hip arthritis
/conditions/hip-arthritis/diet.answer: There is no special hip-arthritis diet, but weight control and an anti-inflammatory pattern matter because extra load on the hip shows up quickly in pain and walking distance.
/conditions/hip-arthritis/diet.bodyHtml:
There is no special hip-arthritis diet, but weight control and an anti-inflammatory pattern matter because extra load on the hip shows up quickly in pain and walking distance.

Foods to favour

  • A Mediterranean-style pattern: oily fish, vegetables, pulses, olive oil
  • Protein at each meal to protect muscle while you strengthen
  • High-fibre carbs that support steady weight loss if needed
  • Calcium-rich foods or fortified alternatives for bone health
  • Water through the day, especially around exercise

Foods to limit

  • Sugary drinks and ultra-processed snacks that make weight loss harder
  • Very large late-night meals if reflux worsens night pain
  • Crash diets that strip muscle you need for the hip
  • Excess alcohol, which disrupts sleep and recovery

Why weight loss helps the hip specifically

Every extra kilogram is multiplied across the hip when you walk or climb stairs. A realistic 5% body-weight reduction often brings a clear drop in day-to-day pain for people with hip OA — more useful than most supplement claims.

Food and NSAIDs

If you use ibuprofen or naproxen for hip flares, take it with food and follow UK safety advice if you have stomach, kidney or heart history. Diet cannot replace that check with a pharmacist or GP.

faqs.q: Is there a special diet for hip arthritis?
faqs.a: No. Weight control and a Mediterranean-style pattern matter because extra load on the hip shows up quickly in pain and walking distance. There is no hip-specific superfood.

faqs.q: Why does weight loss help hip pain?
faqs.a: Each extra kilogram is multiplied across the hip when you walk or climb stairs. A realistic reduction, if you have weight to lose, often helps day-to-day pain more than most supplement claims. Verify any percentage targets with your clinician or a dietitian.

faqs.q: What should I eat around hip exercises?
faqs.a: Protein at meals protects muscle while you strengthen. Drink water around sessions. Crash diets that strip muscle make the joint less supported.

faqs.q: Do glucosamine or collagen fix hip cartilage?
faqs.a: Evidence for rebuilding hip cartilage with supplements is weak. If you still want to try a product, ask a pharmacist about interactions. Food pattern and load on the joint come first.

faqs.q: Can I take pain tablets without food?
faqs.a: Ibuprofen or naproxen for a hip flare should be taken with food. Stomach, kidney or heart history needs a GP or pharmacist check. Diet does not replace that safety step.

/conditions/elbow-arthritis/symptoms.title: Elbow Arthritis Symptoms: Early Signs, Causes & UK Diagnosis Guide | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/symptoms.description: Recognise the early signs of elbow arthritis, common flare-up symptoms, and when to see your GP. Plain-English UK guidance aligned with UK healthcare and NICE
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/symptoms.question: Elbow arthritis symptoms
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/symptoms.answer: Elbow osteoarthritis is less common than hip or knee OA but causes a stiff, aching joint that catches when you straighten or rotate the forearm — often after prior injury or heavy manual work.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/symptoms.bodyHtml:
Elbow osteoarthritis is less common than hip or knee OA but causes a stiff, aching joint that catches when you straighten or rotate the forearm — often after prior injury or heavy manual work.

Common symptoms of elbow arthritis

  • Deep ache around the elbow, worse with gripping or lifting
  • Stiffness, especially first thing or after rest
  • Catching, clicking or locking when straightening the arm
  • Pain turning a door handle, pouring a kettle, or using a screwdriver
  • Swelling or warmth after heavier use
  • Weak grip from pain rather than true nerve damage (though nerve symptoms need a separate check)

When to see your GP

See your GP if elbow pain and stiffness last more than a few weeks, locking is frequent, or you cannot straighten the arm. Mention any old fracture or dislocation of that elbow.

Tennis elbow is not the same as elbow arthritis

Most UK elbow pain is tendon overload on the outside (tennis elbow) or inside (golfer's elbow). True elbow osteoarthritis is less common and more often follows an old fracture or sits inside rheumatoid or psoriatic disease. Outer-elbow pain with gripping and a painful handshake is often tendon, not worn cartilage. Catching, loss of straightening, and a deep joint ache after an old injury point more toward arthritis.

Tingling in the ring and little fingers

Pins and needles in the ring and little fingers with elbow pain can be the ulnar nerve at the inner elbow, not 'just arthritis'. That pattern is worth a GP mention because early activity change and, if needed, nerve-focused care work better than waiting for the fingers to stay numb.

faqs.q: What does elbow arthritis feel like?
faqs.a: A deep ache with stiffness, often worse when straightening or rotating the forearm. Catching or locking is more suggestive of joint surface or loose-body problems than simple tennis elbow.

faqs.q: Is elbow pain always arthritis?
faqs.a: No. Tennis elbow and golfer’s elbow (tendon overload) are more common in UK adults. True elbow osteoarthritis is less common and more often follows an old fracture or inflammatory arthritis.

faqs.q: When should I see a GP about elbow pain?
faqs.a: See a GP if pain and stiffness last more than a few weeks, locking is frequent, you cannot straighten the arm, or you have tingling in the ring and little fingers. Mention any old elbow fracture.

faqs.q: Can elbow arthritis lock the joint?
faqs.a: Yes. Catching, clicking or locking when you straighten the arm can mean the joint surfaces or loose fragments are getting in the way. Repeated locking is a reason to ask about physiotherapy and, if needed, imaging — not to force the arm straight.

faqs.q: Why does my grip feel weak?
faqs.a: Pain often makes you let go of jars and kettles. That is not automatically nerve damage. Numbness in the ring and little fingers is a separate ulnar-nerve clue and should be described to the GP.

/conditions/elbow-arthritis/treatment.title: Elbow Arthritis Treatment in the UK: UK healthcare Options, Medication & Self-Care | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/treatment.description: Evidence-based elbow arthritis treatment in the UK — UK healthcare pathways, medication options, pain relief and self-management strategies that actually work
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/treatment.question: Elbow arthritis treatment
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/treatment.answer: Most elbow arthritis is managed with activity changes, gentle movement, and short-term pain relief. Injections or surgery are reserved for stubborn locking or disabling pain after conservative care.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/treatment.bodyHtml:
Most elbow arthritis is managed with activity changes, gentle movement, and short-term pain relief. Injections or surgery are reserved for stubborn locking or disabling pain after conservative care.

Treatment approaches

Activity modification

Ease repetitive gripping, heavy lifting and vibration tools during flares.

Physiotherapy

Range-of-motion and forearm strengthening protect the joint without forcing end-range pain.

Pain relief

Topical NSAIDs first-line for many people; oral NSAIDs short-term if appropriate.

Heat before movement

Warm the elbow before exercise or morning tasks to reduce stiffness.

Injection

Steroid injection is occasional for a bad flare — discuss benefits and limits with a clinician.

Surgery

Rarely needed; considered for severe arthritis or mechanical locking that blocks daily life.

NHS care without jumping to surgery

Start with a GP or physiotherapist: keep the elbow moving in a comfortable range, share loads between both hands, and use topical NSAID gel if it is suitable for you. Oral tablets are short courses with food, not an all-day habit. Injection and keyhole clean-up are later options when locking or pain still block dressing and cooking after a proper conservative trial.

Work and hobbies

Vibration tools, heavy single-arm bags, and long screwdriver sessions are common flare triggers. A backpack, two-handed lifts, and paced DIY often help more than a new supplement. If your job is manual, occupational health or a workplace physio can look at tools and rest breaks — that is part of treatment, not a sideline.

faqs.q: What is the best treatment for elbow arthritis in the UK?
faqs.a: Most people improve with activity changes, daily gentle movement, topical NSAID gel if suitable, and physiotherapy. Injections and surgery are for stubborn locking or disabling pain after that conservative care.

faqs.q: Should I rest a painful elbow completely?
faqs.a: Full rest usually stiffens the joint. Ease repetitive gripping, vibration tools and heavy lifting during a flare, but keep comfortable bend-and-straighten and forearm rotation.

faqs.q: Do steroid injections cure elbow arthritis?
faqs.a: No. They can settle a bad flare. Benefits are temporary. Discuss how often they are appropriate with a clinician, especially if you also have tennis elbow.

faqs.q: Is elbow replacement common?
faqs.a: It is used much less often than hip or knee replacement, and lifting limits afterwards are stricter. It is a specialist decision after conservative care has failed.

faqs.q: What helps at work with elbow arthritis?
faqs.a: Two-handed lifts, a backpack instead of a one-shoulder bag, paced DIY, and less vibration-tool time. Occupational health can look at tools if your job is manual.

/conditions/elbow-arthritis/exercises.title: Best Exercises for Elbow Arthritis: Safe UK Physio-Aligned Routines | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/exercises.description: Safe, effective elbow arthritis exercises aligned with UK physiotherapy guidance. Movements to try, exercises to avoid, and how to build a weekly routine.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/exercises.question: Best exercises for elbow arthritis
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/exercises.answer: Keep the elbow moving through comfortable range and strengthen the forearm gradually. Avoid grinding into sharp catching pain.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/exercises.bodyHtml:
Keep the elbow moving through comfortable range and strengthen the forearm gradually. Avoid grinding into sharp catching pain.

Key benefits

  • Maintains bend and straighten range for dressing and cooking
  • Improves grip strength for jars and kettles
  • Reduces morning stiffness with daily gentle work
  • Supports recovery after a flare without total rest
  • Pairs well with activity changes at work or hobbies

A simple daily set

Supported bend-and-straighten, palm-up and palm-down rotations, and light grip squeezes (a soft ball) cover most daily function. Heat for a few minutes first if the joint is stiff. Stop short of a sharp catch or lock. If a move repeatedly locks the elbow, skip it and ask a physiotherapist rather than forcing end range.

What to avoid in a flare

Heavy curls, weighted extensions, and pushing through a lock usually worsen swelling. Rest is relative: keep gentle range, drop load, and return to strength when warmth and catching settle.

faqs.q: What are the best exercises for elbow arthritis?
faqs.a: Supported bend-and-straighten, palm-up and palm-down rotations, and light grip squeezes. Warm the elbow first if it is stiff. Stay inside a comfortable range.

faqs.q: Is it safe to exercise with elbow osteoarthritis?
faqs.a: Yes for most people, as long as you stop short of a sharp catch or lock. Heat before movement often reduces morning stiffness.

faqs.q: What exercises should I avoid with elbow arthritis?
faqs.a: Heavy curls, weighted extensions, and pushing through a lock during a flare. Return to load when warmth and catching settle.

faqs.q: How often should I move the elbow?
faqs.a: Short sessions most days beat a long painful workout. Two or three sets of gentle range, plus light grip work on non-flare days, is a realistic pattern.

faqs.q: Can exercise stop elbow arthritis getting worse?
faqs.a: Exercise will not regrow cartilage, but keeping range and forearm strength protects dressing, cooking and lifting better than rest. Pair it with activity changes at work.

/conditions/elbow-arthritis/diet.title: Best Diet for Elbow Arthritis: Anti-Inflammatory Foods to Eat & Avoid (UK) | Living With Arthritis UK
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/diet.description: What to eat — and what to limit — with elbow arthritis. UK-aligned anti-inflammatory diet guidance, food triggers, and the supplements with the best evidence.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/diet.question: Diet for elbow arthritis
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/diet.answer: Diet will not rebuild worn elbow cartilage, but steady weight control, protein for muscle, and an anti-inflammatory pattern support the whole-joint plan.
/conditions/elbow-arthritis/diet.bodyHtml:
Diet will not rebuild worn elbow cartilage, but steady weight control, protein for muscle, and an anti-inflammatory pattern support the whole-joint plan.

Foods to favour

  • Oily fish or omega-3 sources most weeks
  • Lean protein to support forearm and upper-body strength work
  • Fruit, vegetables, pulses and wholegrains
  • Water around exercise sessions

Foods to limit

  • Ultra-processed snacks that crowd out useful meals
  • Excess alcohol
  • Very high-dose supplement stacks marketed for 'cartilage repair' without evidence

Protein around rehab, not miracle cartilage food

Forearm and grip work needs enough protein across the day. A Mediterranean-style pattern is the usual UK-aligned base. No single food rebuilds elbow cartilage. Skip supplement stacks sold as cartilage repair unless your GP or pharmacist has a reason for a specific product.

Tablets and meals

If you use ibuprofen or naproxen for an elbow flare, take it with food. A history of ulcers, kidney or heart disease is a pharmacist or GP check, not a diet-forum question. Gel on the joint often comes first for elbow pain because the joint is close to the skin.

faqs.q: Is there a diet that rebuilds elbow cartilage?
faqs.a: No. A Mediterranean-style pattern, enough protein for strength work, and a healthy weight support the plan. Ignore supplement stacks sold as cartilage repair unless a clinician recommended a specific product.

faqs.q: What should I eat for elbow rehab?
faqs.a: Protein across meals to support forearm and grip work, plus vegetables, pulses, wholegrains and oily fish most weeks. Drink water around exercise.

faqs.q: Should I take ibuprofen on an empty stomach for elbow pain?
faqs.a: No. Take oral NSAIDs with food if they are appropriate for you. Gel on the joint often comes first because the elbow is close to the skin.

faqs.q: Do omega-3 supplements help elbow arthritis?
faqs.a: Oily fish most weeks is the food-first option. High-dose capsules are a pharmacist conversation if you take other medicines. They will not unlock a catching elbow on their own.

faqs.q: Can alcohol make elbow pain worse?
faqs.a: Heavy drinking disrupts sleep and recovery. It is not a specific elbow poison, but poorer sleep makes pain feel worse the next day.
